query: In Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs phase stability and why, with relevance to retaining desirable combinations of high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness? Specify a controlled comparison, predicted observations relative to a baseline, the boundaries of the hypothesis, supporting prior evidence, and an observation that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys, phase stability at 900–1100 °C is governed primarily by the formation of Al-rich B2-type short-range-ordered (SRO) clusters whose volume fraction rises steeply once the average valence-electron concentration (VEC) falls below ≈8.0 e⁻ atom⁻¹; these coherent B2 nanoclusters impede long-range diffusion and dislocation glide, thereby simultaneously (i) delaying decomposition into brittle σ or μ phases, (ii) preserving a dominant FCC matrix that supplies cryogenic toughness, and (iii) providing precipitation strengthening that is retained after irradiation or high-temperature exposure.
generation.material_initial_state: Homogeneous single-phase FCC CoCrFeNi solid solution produced by arc-melting, homogenised at 1200 °C × 24 h, water-quenched.
generation.intervention: Add incremental Al (0, 2, 5, 8, 12 at %) to form CoCrFeNiAlx (x = 0–12 at %), then age all compositions isothermally at 1000 °C for 100 h in vacuum.
generation.conditions: Annealing/aging at 1000 ± 5 °C for 100 h followed by water quench; tests conducted at room temperature, 77 K, and 800 °C in air; ion irradiation with 3 MeV Ni²⁺ to 10 dpa at 500 °C for radiation-tolerance assessment.
generation.structural_mediator: Coherent Al-rich B2 (CsCl) nano-clusters / precipitates (<15 nm) embedded in the FCC matrix.
generation.mechanism: When VEC < ≈8.0, electronic stabilization of the B2 structure allows Al-Ni(Co) pairs to self-organise into nanoscale ordered regions. These regions (a) lower the chemical potential difference between FCC and σ/μ phases, kinetically retarding their nucleation, (b) act as obstacles to dislocation motion and climb, enhancing high-temperature strength, and (c) trap point defects generated by irradiation, improving radiation tolerance, while their coherency with FCC maintains ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the 0 at % Al baseline: • Alloys with 5–8 at % Al will show (i) XRD superlattice reflections (B2), (ii) 25–40 % higher 0.2 % proof stress at 800 °C, (iii) unchanged or <10 % reduction in room-temperature and 77 K elongation to failure, and (iv) ≥50 % lower irradiation defect cluster density. • At ≥12 at % Al the B2 nano-clusters coarsen and transform partially to σ, causing embrittlement and loss of toughness.
generation.baseline: Equiatomic CoCrFeNi (0 at % Al) aged identically, expected to remain single-phase FCC with no B2 SRO and therefore lower 800 °C yield strength (~300 MPa) and higher irradiation defect density.
generation.boundary: Valid for total Al additions 3–10 at %, bulk VEC 7.8–8.2, aging temperatures 900–1100 °C, and cooling rates ≥10 K s⁻¹; outside these ranges (higher Al, slower cooling, VEC >8.3) other intermetallics (σ, BCC) dominate and the hypothesis may not hold.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of strength increment and exact VEC threshold may vary with minor impurities and thermal history; coherency of B2 clusters assumed but must be verified; radiation response extrapolated from analogous systems and remains to be demonstrated directly.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare CoCrFeNiAlx alloys (x = 0, 5, 8 at %) per above, age at 1000 °C × 100 h, quench, then: (1) characterise nanostructure by synchrotron XRD (detect B2 superlattice peaks), atom-probe tomography (measure Al-Ni/Co clustering and coherency), and HRTEM; (2) measure 0.2 % proof stress at 800 °C; (3) assess cryogenic (77 K) Charpy impact toughness; (4) irradiate to 10 dpa at 500 °C and quantify defect cluster density via TEM.
measurements: Volume fraction & size distribution of B2 clusters from APT/TEM
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if alloys with 5–8 at % Al either (a) show no detectable B2 SRO/precipitates OR (b) fail to exceed the 0 at % Al alloy in 800 °C proof stress by at least 10 % while retaining ≥90 % of its cryogenic toughness OR (c) exhibit equal or higher irradiation defect densities relative to the Al-free baseline.
